summary.text: 62-year-old man with prior CABG, referred for pulmonary vein isolation for symptomatic paroxysmal AF; no history of kidney disease, normal examination and TTE, and a large 37 mm left common pulmonary vein ostium on pre-procedural CT.

Pulsed field ablation PVI (35 mm Farapulse catheter, deep sedation with propofol and esketamine, 40 applications, all veins isolated) was completed; he recovered on the ward and was discharged the same afternoon.

That evening he developed cola-coloured urine; after delayed contact he was advised to drink at least 3 L per day. At next-day follow-up the urine colour had normalized but urine output had decreased, he felt unwell and had gained 3 kg, and he was advised to attend the emergency department.

Emergency laboratory evaluation 2 days after PVI showed acute kidney injury (creatinine 713 µmol/L, eGFR 6, urea 21,3), with normal haptoglobin, mildly elevated LDH, urinary haemoglobin 3+, protein 2+ and a few pigmented granular casts; renal ultrasound excluded obstruction.

Treatment comprised IV fluids, bumetanide (stopped when anuria developed) and four temporary haemodialysis sessions. Urine output resumed about one week after the procedure, he was discharged two weeks after admission without further dialysis, and renal function returned to baseline values by 2 months after admission.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not equate the two anchors or call the follow-up values normal; the main-text anchor is used for the recovery event.

evidence.quote: Intracardiac echocardiography was used to confirm adequate catheter-tissue contact throughout the procedure.

In this case, even though the total number of applications was within a moderate range, the combination of possible suboptimal catheter-tissue contact in a large common ostium and a potentially low intravascular volume state may have contributed to red blood cell lysis and impaired haemoglobin clearance; however, it cannot be excluded that additional, as yet unidentified, factors also played a role.

ambiguities.issue: Case text says ICE confirmed adequate contact throughout; the discussion proposes possible suboptimal contact, localized haemolysis and possible low intravascular volume as hypotheses.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not record suboptimal contact, localized haemolysis, fasting, hypovolaemia or pigment nephropathy as patient facts; volume status and fasting are not documented for this patient.
